correctness.rationale: For n>=4, row-or-column coverage proves maximum minimal domination size n and one per column with a missing row. All legal optimum swaps change within one column, so jumping=sliding. Inclusion-exclusion and degree sum yield vertices and edges. Explicit paths cover same-support, constant-to-two-letter, and two-support intersection cases; a first symbol-extinction argument proves the matching diameter lower bound. Independently implemented direct graph enumeration for n=4..7 and complete word-graph BFS for n=4..9 pass, as secondary finite checks.

evidence: B. Brešar, Vizing-like conjecture for the upper domination of Cartesian products of graphs—the proof, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 12 (2005), N12, DOI 10.37236/1979 (first public 2005-07-19). Establishes a general product inequality, not an exchange graph or its exact metric.

A. Suzuki, A. E. Mouawad and N. Nishimura, Reconfiguration of Dominating Sets, arXiv:1401.5714 (first posted 2014-01-22). Considers token addition/removal rather than fixed-cardinality exchange on only maximum inclusion-minimal dominating sets.

H. AbouEisha et al., Upper Domination: towards a dichotomy through boundary properties, arXiv:1609.01510 (first posted 2016-09-06). Addresses upper-domination algorithmics and graph classes, not the exact state space and sharp exchange diameter.

R. Burdett, M. Haythorpe and A. Newcombe, Binary programming formulations for the upper domination problem, Math. Methods Oper. Res. 98 (2023), DOI 10.1007/s00186-023-00831-2. Discusses integer formulations and numerical rook instances, not this optimum-exchange theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known numerical values Gamma(K_3 square K_n)=n and broad product lower bounds cannot imply classification, exact edge count, token-jump=token-slide identity, or sharp diameter. Graph-family and adjacency-model hypotheses were compared, not just paper titles. No inspected theorem subsumes the claimed four-part result.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of the inspected prior statements implies the metric characterization: Brešar gives inequality of optima, not state-space structure; Suzuki permits intermediary sizes and nonminimal states; complexity and formulation papers address decision/optimization, and related mathematical records concern other parameters. evidence: The reconfiguration graph is the Hamming graph on non-surjective ternary words; its exact vertex count is 3*2^n-3, its edge count 3n(2^(n-1)+1), and its diameter n+floor(n/2)-1. No matching equivalent formulation was returned by the cited semantic queries.
Suzuki et al., arXiv:1401.5714, analyze reconfiguration of all bounded-cardinality dominating sets under add/remove rather than single replacement among maximum inclusion-minimal sets.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Also searched the exact word-reconfiguration alias and checked the implications of a general Hamming bound: the ambient diameter n does NOT imply the induced, three-letter-nonsurjective subgraph diameter. Non-surjective and omitted-symbol formulations were explicitly compared; absent matching search hits alone is not proof of priority.

originality.rationale: Extensive primary-source statement comparison and publicly indexed mathematical-record searches found no equivalent whole theorem. Known upper-domination numerical values and product inequality do not imply exact optimum configuration graph nor n+floor(n/2)-1 diameter. Distinct fixed-cardinality minimality and adjacency hypotheses were checked against Suzuki et al. Search incompleteness and unindexed priority remain risks.
residual_risks: General reconfiguration literature is broad; an unindexed result about non-surjective ternary Hamming words may give the same diameter under different vocabulary.
Historical claims available here and primary mathematical literature may not exhaust unpublished, inaccessible, or otherwise unindexed work.
Well-dominated product literature was screened at a high level, not relied upon for a full-text exclusion; it is not a demonstrated implication of the new theorem.

value.rationale: The full optimum state space of a canonical Cartesian rook family is classified; the restrictive sliding and jumping models coincide, with an explicit graph-size and sharp metric theorem. The diameter n+floor(n/2)-1 exceeds the unconstrained Hamming diameter by almost 50%, a structurally motivated transport obstruction not given by Gamma=n or counts alone. This supplies a general geometric invariant with applications to rearrangement of extremal minimal dominating sets.
